carol-pm: Quick sync: drafting a 'graceful regional eviction' spec that explicitly compares opt-in reserved pools vs per-tenant opt-outs. Objective: predictable behavior during regional pressure, clear pricing path, minimal surprise for customers. Sketch below.

diego-eng: We should define concrete actions and order of operations. My ordered list: 1) lightweight context trim (no model change), 2) token rate limit, 3) quantized-model variant, 4) cross-region reroute to same-class model, 5) best-effort stub.

carol-pm: Proposed workflow: detect congestion -> shadow detection -> try context trim (short window) -> escalate every X minutes; if a tenant is exempt, route to reserved pool if available.

maya-sre: Telemetry & safety: require region_p95, region_error_rate, GPU_util, and tenant_p95. Auto-trigger if region_p95 > baseline + 200ms for 90s AND GPU_util > 85% for 60s. Abort and rollback if tenant_error_rate > 1% for 3m. Record sample set of 100 evicted requests per region.

sam-custops: Customer ask: a few enterprise customers want guaranteed non-eviction during business hours. They asked for an API opt-out and a pricing add-on for reserved capacity. Need clarity on how to surface hours and billing.

oliver-sales: We'll propose two commercial options: 1) free opt-out (manual, best-effort) for small customers, 2) paid Reserved Pool with hard guarantee during specified windows and SLA. Legal/sales to draft contract language.

diego-eng: Flag schema (draft):
```
regional_eviction_mode: off|monitor|trim|throttle|downgrade|reroute|stub
eviction_slice_pct: 0-100
eviction_exempt_tenants: [tenant_ids]
reserved_pool_enabled: bool
reserved_pool_hours: [TZ-aware windows]
eviction_cooldown_seconds: 600
max_evictions_per_region_per_hour: 6
```
Keep flags per-region and allow tenant-level override.

maya-sre: Canary & rollout plan: 1) shadow-only (no user impact) 24h -> 2) 1% traffic in eu-west (15m window) -> 5% (30m) -> 20% (1h). Always run shadow comparisons of outputs for quality delta. Stop rollout if quality delta > threshold or error_rate spikes. Add traffic-replay tests simulating region overload.

carol-pm: Launch must-haves:
- API to set eviction_exempt flag tested
- Reserved pool routing and billing hook validated with sales/legal
- Runbook + panic play + dashboard visible metrics
- Canary shows < 0.5% customer-visible regressions in 48h window

sam-custops: Also need customer comms templates (planned windows + emergency rollback) and a support view that shows tenant fallback state and last eviction time.

maya-sre: Ops checklist: preflight smoke tests per variant, circuit breaker config (eviction_cooldown_seconds), token-bucket limiter to avoid cascading evictions, and an emergency endpoint to disable cross-region reroutes.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: `rollout/regional-eviction/v1` -> canary start 2026-04-20T09:00:00Z (1% eu-west)

diego-eng: I'll open the PR with flag implementation details and the telemetry hooks.

carol-pm: I'll draft the PRD and tag legal + sales for commercial language. Revisit after their feedback. If anyone has critical must-haves, post them here and I'll add to the ticket.
